plain_definition: A set of procedures a financial institution must follow under Bank Secrecy Act regulations to verify each customer's identity before opening an account -- collecting identifying information such as name, address, and taxpayer identification number, and verifying it through documentary or other means. Banks have long been required to maintain one; the GENIUS Act's implementing rulemaking would extend the same kind of requirement to permitted payment stablecoin issuers, a category of company the Act newly created.
formal_definition: 31 CFR 1020.220 sets out the customer identification program requirement currently applicable to banks under the Bank Secrecy Act. The rule proposed here would add a parallel customer identification program requirement for permitted payment stablecoin issuers as part of implementing the GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27).
